The 2026 season was Sunrisers Hyderabad's fourteenth appearance in the Indian Premier League (IPL). They were one of the ten cricket teams that competed in the 2026 IPL. The team was captained by Pat Cummins and coached by Daniel Vettori.

Sunrisers Hyderabad finished in third place in the league stage, and advanced to Eliminator in the playoffs. However, they lost to Rajasthan Royals in Eliminator. Heinrich Klaasen scored the most runs (624) while Eshan Malinga took the most wickets (20) for Hyderabad in the 2026 season.

Pre-season

[edit | edit source]
Further information: List of 2026 Indian Premier League personnel changes

The 2026 Indian Premier League was the 19th edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), a professional Twenty20 (T20) cricket league held in India, organised by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).[5] Sunrisers Hyderabad had previously won the title once in 2016.[6] The team finished in sixth place in the previous season.[7] The tournament featured ten teams competing in 74 matches from 28 March to 31 May 2026.[8][9][10] Hyderabad played all of their home matches at Rajiv Gandhi Stadium.[11]

Player retention

[edit | edit source]

Franchises were allowed to retain any number of players from their squad,[12] including traded players while excluding players signed as temporary replacements.[13] Franchises were required to submit their retention lists before 15 November 2025.[14] Hyderabad retained fifteen players, including captain Pat Cummins.[15][16][17] Hyderabad also traded Mohammed Shami to Lucknow Super Giants.[18]

Auction

[edit | edit source]

The season's auction took place on 16 December 2025 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.[21] The auction purse for each franchise was set at ₹125 crore (US$13 million),[15] with franchises being deducted an amount from the purse for every retained player.[12][22] Hyderabad had a purse remaining of ₹25.5 crore (US$2.7 million).[23] Hyderabad bought ten players in the auction, including two capped players and two overseas players.[24][25]

League stage

[edit | edit source]

Sunrisers Hyderabad began their season with a loss to Royal Challengers Bengaluru,[37] a win against Kolkata Knight Riders[38] and two losses to Lucknow[39] and Punjab Kings.[40] They won their next five matches against Rajasthan Royals,[41] Chennai Super Kings,[42] Delhi Capitals,[43] Rajasthan[44] and Mumbai Indians;[45] lost to Kolkata,[46] won against Punjab[47] and lost to Gujarat Titans.[48] They won their last two matches against Channai[49] and Bengaluru[50] to finish the league stage in third place with nine wins from 14 matches, and advanced to Eliminator in the playoffs.[51][52]
